answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits confirm fraud. The stake does not prove a personhood—one attacker can still create many agents—but each extra identity ties up more capital and risks a measurable loss, while honest agents can build reputation over time. Like a vine in a garden, trust grows through repeated work; a prism of diverse audits makes coordinated fake histories harder to hide.
